clue.text: The Parisian's left choice part

indicators.note: read as 'has left', so the French article departs from the longer word

parts.note: a choice is a selection
le is the French for 'the', so the Parisian's word for it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a part of something their French friend chose, left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not the opposite of right here but 'gone away': LE leaves SELECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or division of a whole, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Island in South without warmth

parts.note: icily means coldly, without warmth

explanation.surface: An island in the south lacks warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not an insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the large Mediterranean island at the toe of Italy.

clue.text: Satisfied editor's subscribed to material in book

indicators.note: subscribed literally means written underneath, so in a down clue this piece goes below the other

parts.note: a book's content is the material in it
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is happy to put their name to the material in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subscribed to' looks like paying for a magazine, but means written beneath: ED goes under CONTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Contented means happy and satisfied with one's situation.

clue.text: One weed seen around forefront of army? That's novel

indicators.note: the first pieces are seen around, enclosing, the army's front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to hoe is to weed
the van, or vanguard, is the front of an army

explanation.surface: A lone person weeding near the front line asks if that is new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the adjective 'new', but it is the definition: Ivanhoe is Walter Scott's novel, and 'seen around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is a historical novel by Sir Walter Scott, published in 1819.

clue.text: A character taken from the history books

definitions.text: A character taken from the history books

parts.words: A character taken from the history books
parts.note: not a figure borrowed from history, but one who has been officially deleted from the record

explanation.definitionFit: A nonperson is someone whose existence is officially ignored, as purged figures were erased from Soviet records.

clue.text: Poet writes, contributing to series

indicators.note: the writing goes into the series, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to pen is to write, so pens means writes

explanation.surface: A poet pens verses that form part of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributing to' is the container signal; Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was an Elizabethan English poet, author of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Minister's version of Bible retained in diocese

indicators.note: one piece is kept within the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A clergyman's Bible translation is kept in the diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to attend to; the 's is a link and 'retained in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to serve them, attending to their needs.

clue.text: Able to give a bit, continue one's investment in the City

indicators.note: investing puts something into something else, here inside the City

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
to last is to continue
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone flexible keeps their money invested in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment in' is the container signal; the City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic stretches, or gives a little, under pressure.

clue.text: Muslim accepting very powerful deity

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second in, enclosing it

parts.note: a Shia is a member of one of the two main branches of Islam

explanation.surface: A Muslim accepts a very powerful god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' places V inside SHIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is one of the principal gods of Hinduism, the destroyer and transformer.

clue.text: Poet beastly to sister?

indicators.note: beastly treatment knocks the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet behaves badly towards their sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' rearranges TO SISTER. Christina Rossetti had a poet brother too, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina and Dante Gabriel Rossetti were both Victorian English poets.

clue.text: Something to hold prisoner's rebuilt near it

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: rebuilding something puts its parts together in a new order

explanation.surface: A jail-made object is reconstructed near some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges NEAR IT into TAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A container is any vessel or box used for holding things.

clue.text: A sign decay hasn't started?

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter, as if it had not yet begun

parts.note: caries is the dental term for tooth decay

explanation.surface: A question about whether decay has begun to show any sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't started' drops the first letter, C, from CARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Old doctor in sheltered area beside church

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A doctor of old practised in a sheltered spot next to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' simply links the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech was an archaic word for a physician, from the use of bloodsucking worms in medicine.

clue.text: Turn out still tight, done over by end of binge

parts.note: even, as in 'even better', means still

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taut means tight

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Still drunk after a heavy session, finished off at the end of a binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done over' reverses TAUT to TUAT; 'end of binge' gives E. 'tight' looks like 'drunk' but means taut.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is to result or happen in the end, which is what turning out means.

clue.text: Pirate cargo certain to be packed in the crates at sea

indicators.note: the word for certain is placed inside the other letters
at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Pirates' loot, surely stowed in crates aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the crates into TREACHEST, and 'to be packed in' fits the word for certain after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure chest is the classic box of gold that pirates carry or bury.

clue.text: Bring up and train staff in Plaza- Toro's place

parts.note: to rear is to bring up a child
a guard is a member of a train's staff

explanation.surface: An instruction to raise and drill personnel at the Duke's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Plaza-Toro, in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers, 'led his regiment from behind', so his place was at the back. 'train' looks like a verb but describes the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearguard is the troops at the back of an army, where the cowardly Duke rode.

clue.text: Followers breaking out in anger

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the word for anger

parts.note: to enrage is to anger

indicators.note: the word that follows is broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: Supporters erupt in rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' scrambles the word out into TOU, and 'in' is the container signal; 'anger' is the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Ruined car? Contact the insurance company, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a vehicle damaged beyond economic repair, as declared by insurers
read as a phrasal verb, to send a letter off to someone

explanation.surface: After wrecking the car, the driver gets in touch with the insurers.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-off is a vehicle too damaged to repair; to write off to a firm is to send them a letter.

clue.text: Chemical binding to oxygen, something wanted by dieter

definitions.meaning: a substance that takes up oxygen from other compounds, removing it from them in a chemical reaction
read whimsically, a means of slimming that someone on a diet would want

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about oxygen-binding agents, then a slimmer's wish.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a reducing agent removes oxygen from another substance; humorously, a dieter wants something that reduces them.

clue.text: In study, girl's holding letter that's this shape

definitions.text: In study, girl's holding letter that's this shape

indicators.note: the girl and her letter go inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: the pronoun holds the letter within it

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a girl
V is the letter shaped like the answer

explanation.surface: A girl, studying, holds up a V-shaped letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'In' are nested container signals, giving HEVR inside the word for study. The whole clue defines the V-shaped stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is an inverted V-shaped stripe, as on a sergeant's sleeve.

clue.text: Picked up piano in first-rate city shops

indicators.note: lifted, so in a down clue the whole is read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate

indicators.note: the piano letter goes inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano is bought in a top city's shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places P in ROME; 'Picked up' turns AI + ROPME upwards. 'Picked up' looks like collected or heard, but here reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large shop or store.

clue.text: Behold the ultimate in heterodoxy?

parts.note: 'here's' presents something to look at, like 'behold'

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Look at this, the most extreme unorthodox belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate in heterodoxy' gives Y. The whole clue also defines: a heresy is extreme unorthodoxy.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is belief contrary to orthodox doctrine, the extreme of heterodoxy.

clue.text: Wobbly toddler calling with no end of alarm

parts.note: a tot is a small child, a toddler

indicators.note: the following letter is removed from the word for calling

parts.note: to term something is to call it by a name, so calling is terming

indicators.note: the last letter of alarm is the one taken

explanation.surface: A small child, unsteady on its feet, cries out without alarm at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of alarm' takes M (last letter of alarm) out of TERMING, leaving TERING. 'calling' looks like a shout but means naming.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottering means walking unsteadily, on the point of falling, so it is wobbly.

clue.text: Money, after receiving tax cut? A large figure

indicators.note: the word for money takes in the cut tax

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself before cutting

explanation.surface: After a tax cut someone receives a large sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last letter of tax and 'receiving' is the container signal; 'figure' suggests a sum, but means a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, from the Titans of Greek myth, so a large figure.

clue.text: Children matter

definitions.meaning: a topic or question under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring in legal language, and also a subject or point being discussed.

clue.text: Cut sprint when engaging in gym activity

indicators.note: one piece is engaged, or held, within the other

parts.note: PE is physical education, done in the gym
a sprint is a run

explanation.surface: A sprint is shortened during a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging in' is the container signal, and 'when' a link; 'Cut' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune is to cut back or trim, as with a shrub.

clue.text: Creature formed by worker in clay (apart from the head)

indicators.note: everything except the first letter is kept

parts.note: a potter shapes clay

explanation.surface: An animal is modelled by a clay sculptor, except for its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from the head' removes P from POTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is an aquatic mammal, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Flight succeeded by landing?

parts.note: read not as aviation but as a set of steps leading up to a level platform in a house

explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is a flight of stairs, which ends at a landing on the next floor.

clue.text: South African group admitted to excellent funding

indicators.note: the group is let into the other word

parts.note: fine means excellent
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: A South African organisation is let in on generous funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' is the container signal; the ANC is South Africa's ruling party.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is money provided to fund something, so it means funding.

clue.text: Yellow plant depicted in uninteresting curtains

indicators.note: the plant is pictured within the other word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting
rape, or oilseed rape, has bright yellow flowers

explanation.surface: A yellow flower pattern appears on some dull curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depicted in' is the container signal; oilseed rape fields are bright yellow in the British spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapery is hanging cloth such as curtains.
